title: Pick Defined Fields
prompt: A TypeScript API patch should only send fields that were actually provided. Write a function that returns a new object with keys whose values are not undefined. Keep null, false, 0, and empty strings because those are intentional values.

explanation.beginner:
Example: pickDefined({"name":"Ada"}) produces {"name":"Ada"}. The result must follow this precise rule: A TypeScript API patch should only send fields that were actually provided. Write a function that returns a new object with keys whose values are not undefined. Keep null, false, 0, and empty strings because those are intentional values. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “keeps intentional falsy values”: input [{"active":false,"count":0,"note":""}] produces {"active":false,"count":0,"note":""}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.
